summary: PHILEON Behavioral Customer Retention (Simulation Mode) — backend-only verification. tests/test_retention_behavioral.py: 30/31 PASS, 1 DETERMINISTIC FAIL (test_unsub_token_roundtrip) due to a real bug in services.retention_service.make_unsub_token / verify_unsub_token token format — the code joins body + b'.' + sig then base64-encodes, and verify uses raw.rsplit(b'.', 1). Because sig is 32 raw HMAC-SHA256 bytes it can (and here does) contain 0x2e ('.') bytes, so rsplit finds the WRONG separator and HMAC compare_digest fails. The main agent's local 31/31 pass is timestamp/secret dependent (probabilistic ~1 - (1-1/256)^32 ≈ 12% failure rate per token). Broader regression suites requested all still green: test_customer_experience_phase 23/23, test_shipping_integrity_email + notification_state, test_stripe_hardening, test_bnpl_cad_lane, test_bnpl_payment_methods — 93/93 combined. Public URL sanity: POST /api/behavior/events (minimal)→202, with customer_email key→422 (extra=forbid), ORDER_PAID event_type→422, /api/behavior/newsletter/subscribe bad email→400, /api/admin/retention/pending no-auth→403, GET /api/unsubscribe?token=tampered→HTTP 400 rendering HTML 'UNABLE TO VERIFY LINK.' page. Identity-safety + admin-auth surfaces confirmed at ingress. STRIPE_MODE=test and PHILEON_BEHAVIORAL_LIVE unset preserved.

critical.issue: Token format uses b'.' as separator between body and 32-byte raw HMAC sig BEFORE base64 encoding, but sig can (and in the deterministic test vector DOES) contain 0x2e bytes. verify_unsub_token()'s raw.rsplit(b'.', 1) then splits at the wrong '.', body includes trailing sig bytes, sig becomes truncated, hmac.compare_digest returns False, and a legitimate token returns None. Repro: JWT_SECRET='test-secret-for-retention', email='hello@x.com' → make_unsub_token(...) → verify_unsub_token(token) returns None. Bug is probabilistic (~12% per token) so main-agent smoke can be green while the pytest vector fails deterministically. This is a real launch-blocker for behavioral unsubscribe reliability — ~1 in 8 emailed unsubscribe links will silently render 'UNABLE TO VERIFY LINK' even though the recipient clicked their own valid link.

action_items: Fix services/retention_service.py token codec. Recommended minimal fix: use a separator that cannot appear in either half, e.g. urlsafe-b64encode body and sig SEPARATELY and join with '.' as ASCII text (b64 alphabet excludes '.'), OR change binary joiner to b'||' plus a length prefix, OR hex-encode sig before joining. Example: `return b64u(body).rstrip('=') + '.' + b64u(sig).rstrip('=')` and split on ASCII '.' in verify. Add a regression test that runs the roundtrip 200x with random secrets/emails to guarantee no probabilistic gap remains.
critical_code_review_comments: retention_service.make_unsub_token: joining raw HMAC sig with a b'.' delimiter and base64-encoding the union is unsafe — 32 random sig bytes have a substantial (~12%) probability of containing 0x2e, and rsplit('.', 1) is order-sensitive to that. Root cause is mixing text-space delimiters with binary-space payloads. Fix by delimiting in text space after b64 encoding each half.

routes/behavior.py POST /api/behavior/events correctly rejects customer_email/email/user_id via Pydantic extra='forbid' (verified via public URL → 422) — impersonation surface from public browser is closed.
routes/behavior.py POST /api/behavior/events correctly rejects ORDER_PAID as an event_type from the public endpoint (verified → 422). Webhook-only invariant preserved.
routes/admin_retention.py requires verify_admin (verified public URL → 403 without JWT). No accidental public exposure.

GET /api/unsubscribe correctly returns HTML 'UNABLE TO VERIFY LINK.' page for tampered tokens with noindex,nofollow meta and no internal-field leakage. Good posture. Only the underlying verifier's probabilistic failure (see critical) reduces the effective success rate of legitimate links.
Simulation-mode invariant holds in unit path: tick returns mode='simulated' and behavior_send_log rows carry mode='simulated' when PHILEON_BEHAVIORAL_LIVE is unset (30/31 covering these paths PASS).

Regression bar preserved: 93/93 across test_customer_experience_phase, test_shipping_integrity_email, test_shipping_integrity_notification_state, test_stripe_hardening, test_bnpl_cad_lane, test_bnpl_payment_methods. No collateral impact from behavioral phase code.
test_credentials: Admin JWT obtainable via `python -c 'from server import create_token; print(create_token("admin"))'` (not needed for the failing test — it is a pure in-process HMAC roundtrip).
seed_data_creation: None. Public URL smoke used ephemeral session_id 'testsess1' with no persistence commitment beyond a single 202-accepted anonymous PRODUCT_VIEWED event (30-day TTL applies).
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent fixes make_unsub_token/verify_unsub_token to use text-space delimiter or separately-b64-encoded halves, rerun `pytest tests/test_retention_behavioral.py -v` and expect 31/31. Also worth adding a random-fuzz roundtrip (200 iterations) to permanently gate against the sig-contains-0x2e class of bug. Everything else in the behavioral phase (event ingestion, intent hierarchy, cancellation on ORDER_PAID, anon TTL + bind unset, consent gate, simulation-mode invariant, admin auth, public identity forbid, email builder scarcity/leak checks) is green.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: `JWT_SECRET='test-secret-for-retention'; from services import retention_service as R; t = R.make_unsub_token('hello@x.com'); assert R.verify_unsub_token(t) == 'hello@x.com'` → AssertionError (returns None). Decoded raw token bytes: b'hello@x.com|1796404672.=@\x80\x894\x1cD\xba\xd4\xa6\xf7-\xde\xa3\x03\xd1\xdf\x16X\x04\xa5\xf3.\tB,J\xa6\x96\xa3\x17\xfe' — contains THREE 0x2e bytes; rsplit(b'.', 1) picks the last one (inside the HMAC sig), yielding a body that includes 22 sig bytes and a truncated 10-byte sig → HMAC compare fails → verify returns None. Mitigation: change the codec so the separator lives in text space (post-b64) or use a delimiter impossible in either half (e.g. length-prefixed framing, or independently b64-encode body and sig and join with '.'). Do NOT rotate JWT_SECRET as a workaround — the flaw is structural and will recur with any secret.
